title: Mutable vs Immutable Types in Python

scenes.line1: Can lists change but tuples can't?
scenes.say: Ever wonder why lists can change but tuples can't? Let's see why this matters for your next Python interview.
Mutable types, like lists and dictionaries, can be changed after they're made. Immutable types, like tuples and strings, stay the same forever.
Here's a classic gotcha. If you assign a list to another name and change it, both names see the update. That's because both point to the same object.

scenes.label: Copy
scenes.sub: Use deep copy to avoid shared changes.
scenes.say: If you want a true independent copy, use a deep copy. That way, changes in one won't affect the other.

scenes.question: Does assignment copy an object?
scenes.right: No, assignment just binds a name to the same object.
scenes.say: Here's a common interview trap: Assignment doesn't copy the object. It just gives you another name for the same thing.
